topic: 学术综合任务与转段检查 · Independent new scenario: a seminar revising a hypothesis after conflicting findings
grammarFocus: 根据个人错题复查时态、从句、冠词、数量和主谓一致。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: The Seminar That Changed Its Mind
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思试题，也不代表任何官方分数。请先通读文章，完成10道阅读题；然后学习语法讲解并完成8道语法题；最后完成口语与写作任务。所有题目答案均可在文中找到依据。
passage:
Last Tuesday, the research seminar in Room 204 met to discuss a small study on study habits. The group had collected data for six weeks. Their hypothesis was simple: students who study in short, frequent sessions remember more than students who study in one long session. The seminar leader, Dr. Chen, asked the group to look at the results carefully.

A. The first finding surprised everyone. The short-session group did better on a weekly quiz, but the long-session group did better on a final test. "That is not what we expected," said Marco, a second-year student. "Our hypothesis predicted one clear winner." The group checked the data again. The numbers were correct. The result was real, but it was not simple. This mixed pattern suggested that the two types of study might support different kinds of memory or performance. For example, short sessions may help students recall specific facts quickly, while longer sessions may allow deeper processing of complex ideas. However, the group could not be sure yet, because other factors might have influenced the results.

B. Dr. Chen asked a question: "What if the two groups studied in different ways?" The group looked at their notes. The short-session group often studied in the morning. The long-session group usually studied at night. Also, the long-session group took longer breaks during study. These differences were not part of the original plan. The group had not controlled them. In research, such uncontrolled variables can affect the outcome and make it difficult to know which factor caused the difference. For instance, studying at night might suit some students better, or longer breaks might reduce fatigue and improve focus. Because these variables were not controlled, the group could not confidently attribute the quiz and test results to session length alone.

C. The seminar then revised its hypothesis. The new hypothesis was: short, frequent sessions help students remember facts for a short time, but long sessions with breaks help students understand ideas for a longer time. The group agreed that this new idea fit the data better. They also agreed to run a new study with better controls. This would involve randomly assigning participants to groups, keeping study times consistent, and standardizing break lengths. By controlling these factors, the group hoped to isolate the effect of session length and better understand how different study patterns influence learning.

At the end of the meeting, Dr. Chen said, "A hypothesis is not a promise. It is a question we ask the data. When the data answers differently, we listen." The group left with a new plan and a better question.

grammar.title: 时态、从句、冠词、数量与主谓一致复习
grammar.explanation: 本课重点复习五类常见错误：1) 时态：过去完成时表示过去某一时间之前完成的动作，如 'had collected'；一般过去时表示过去发生的动作，如 'met'。2) 从句：宾语从句用陈述语序，如 'what we expected'，不用疑问语序。3) 冠词：特指用 the，泛指用 a/an，不可数或泛指复数用零冠词。4) 数量：可数名词复数用 many/few，不可数用 much/little；'a number of' 接复数，'the number of' 接单数。5) 主谓一致：主语为单数第三人称时动词加 -s；'each'、'everyone' 作主语用单数；'the group' 视为单数。请先理解规则，再完成8道新句子练习。
grammar.example: The group had collected data for six weeks.

questions.prompt: By the time the seminar started, the group ______ the data.
questions.explanation: 表示在过去开始之前已完成的动作，用过去完成时 had collected。
questions.evidence: The group had collected data for six weeks.

questions.prompt: She asked me ______ the results were correct.
questions.explanation: 宾语从句表示“是否”用 whether，语序为陈述语序。
questions.evidence: Dr. Chen asked a question: "What if the two groups studied in different ways?"

questions.prompt: I was surprised by ______ answer Marco gave.
questions.explanation: 特指 Marco 给出的那个答案，用定冠词 the。
questions.evidence: That is not what we expected.

questions.prompt: There are ______ students in the seminar today than yesterday.
questions.explanation: students 是可数名词复数，比较级用 fewer。
questions.evidence: The group left with a new plan and a better question.

questions.prompt: Each of the students ______ a different opinion.
questions.explanation: Each of + 复数名词作主语时，谓语用单数 has。
questions.evidence: The group agreed that this new idea fit the data better.

questions.explanation: The number of 作主语表示数量，谓语用单数 was。

questions.prompt: He said that he ______ the data twice.
questions.explanation: 主句为过去时，从句表示更早发生的动作，用过去完成时 had checked。
questions.evidence: The group checked the data again.

questions.prompt: ______ information in the report is useful.
questions.explanation: information 不可数，特指报告中的信息，用 the；many 不能修饰不可数名词。
questions.evidence: The group looked at their notes.

transfer.writing: Write a short paragraph (120–150 words) about a time when you had to change a plan because of new information. Explain what the original plan was, what new information you found, and what you changed. Use at least two past perfect sentences and one object clause.
